reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 69 --verse 7.33.7: Sāyaṇa’s own gloss reads the three as agnivāyusūryāḥ in pṛthivy-antarikṣa-dyu (earth, mid-air, sky) in order, and the gharmāsaḥ as the same three; he then cites the Śāṭyāyanaka (tathā ca śāṭyāyanakam) naming the three peoples vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ. The sentence puts ‘citing the Śāṭyāyanaka’ before the whole reading, so the Vasus/Rudras/Ādityas part (not in his own gloss) is attributed to the text he quotes; Wilson’s note (‘Sayana quotes Satyayana’) confirms. Evidence verbatim. day.js: 7.33 is on the Vasisthas, the Ten Kings, and Vasistha’s birth (10 to 13); ‘threefold lore’ is a light gloss of ‘all these have they discovered’, no four-word run. ‘Aryan’ avoided.
